## GameInfo / HowToPlay Popup

### Description
The InfoPopup component can be used to display the HowToPlay and GameInfo screens. It builds on the GraphicalSlideManager from the slider package to add a fade overlay over the game and a close button aswell as enhancing the open and close methods to create a consistent experience across games.
Combined with the [`InstructionSlide`](./instruction-slide.md) component, we can rapidly create a consistent How To Play expreience in every game.

### Basic Usage
```ts
// You'll first need to create an array of slides to display in the popup.
import { ImageSlide, InstructionSlide, Slide } from '@arcade-client/base-package';

const htpSlides: Slide[] = [
    new ImageSlide(AssetManager.getTextureResourceData('htp-screen-1')),
    new InstructionSlide(AssetManager.getTextureResourceData('htp-screen-2'), container.strings.howToPlay.slides[1])
];
```
`ImageSlide` and [`InstructionSlide`](./instruction-slide.md) have been created to quickly build simple/common slide layouts.
Custom slide layouts can be built by extending `Slide`.

```ts
import { InfoPopup } from '@arcade-client/base-package';

// Initialise the component passing in the initial set of slides and the required textures
const infoPopup = new InfoPopup(
    htpSlides,
    {
        background: AssetManager.getTextureResourceData('htp-bg'),
        arrow: AssetManager.getTextureResourceData('htp-arrow'),
        close: AssetManager.getTextureResourceData('htp-cross')
    }
    // a config can be passed here for fine detail tweaks, see below
);

// Then add it to the stage so it can be seen
GameApplication.pixiApp.stage.addChild(infoPopup);

// Then call show when you want it to display
infoPopup.show();

// Be sure to call resize on things like orientation change
infoPopup.resize(width, height);
```

#### Detecting the popup closing
The show function returns a Promise which resolves when it is closed. Allowing you to open the popup and wait for it to be closed before resuming execution.
```ts
// Example using the Promise to wait for the popup to be closed
await this.infoPopup.show();
console.log('the info popup has been closed');
```

#### Changing Slides
You can optionally pass in an array of slides for it to display when calling `show()`. Calling `show()` without passing anything in will show the slides last set (which will be the ones passed in to the constructor on the first call).
```ts
// Example using the built in HTP and GameInfo events to show the popup with different slides when a user opens those
eventEmitter.on(events.POPUP.TOGGLE_HTP_POPUP, () => infoPopup.show(htpSlides), infoPopup);
eventEmitter.on(events.POPUP.TOGGLE_GAME_INFO, () => infoPopup.show(gameInfoSlides), infoPopup);
```

#### Config
The various features and settings default to the standard behaviour we expect across our games (such as transition times, auto-transition, arrow visibility, etc...) however these can be changed via the config if required.
The config also contains values to adjust visual things like padding and component scales. To help keep things looking correct across a variety of asset designs.
```ts
interface IGraphicalSlideManConfig {
    features?: Partial<ISliderFeatures>;
    arrowScale?: number;
    arrowXOffset?: number;
    xPadding?: number;
    slideWidthMultiplier?: number;
    slideHeightMultiplier?: number;
    slideYOffsetMultiplier?: number;
    slideXOffsetMultiplier?: number;
    arrowVisibilityCallback?: () => boolean;
}
```
```ts
interface ISliderFeatures {
    transitionTimes: {
        manual: number;
        auto: number;
    };
    swipeTransition: {
        enabled: boolean;
    };
    controlsTextures?: {
        enabled: Texture;
        disabled: Texture;
    };
    autoTransition?: {
        slideChangeTime: number;
    };
}
```
